title: Why [[0]*3]*3 shares one row
question: List comprehension or NumPy array?
fact_source: https://docs.python.org/3/faq/programming.html#how-do-i-create-a-multidimensional-list and https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#common-sequence-operations (note 2: items in s*n are referenced multiple times, not copied; [[0]*3]*3 makes 3 references to one list; fix: [[0]*3 for _ in range(3)])

scenes.headline: One write changed three rows
scenes.voice: You set one cell in your grid, and all three rows change?
scenes.caption: You set one cell in your grid, and all 3 rows change?

scenes.headline: * 3 copies the reference
scenes.voice: Times three copies the reference, not the list. All three rows are the same inner list.
scenes.caption: * 3 copies the reference, not the list. All 3 rows are the same inner list.

scenes.headline: Build each row fresh
scenes.voice: Build each row fresh with a list comprehension, using for underscore in range of three.
scenes.caption: Build each row fresh with a list comprehension: for _ in range(3).

scenes.headline: 1 write = 1 cell
scenes.voice: Now one write changes one cell, not three. Three rows, three separate lists.
scenes.caption: Now 1 write changes 1 cell, not 3. Three rows, three separate lists.

scenes.voice: For a grid, which do you use: a list comprehension, or a NumPy array? Comment your answer.
scenes.caption: For a grid, which do you use: a list comprehension, or a NumPy array? Comment your answer.
